comments: Same recipe as kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_kernel3_finetune_dropout.json (kernel3 + finetune + dropout), retrained under quant.py's leaky slope=0.125 and the 2*w_stored+1 weight-multiplication hardware scheme (both new). First attempt at this combo (quant_freeze_iters=60000, same as the original 0.1/w=w anchor) collapsed to trivial all-background prediction (dice ~0.2499) by epoch 285/300, well after its own val-dice peak of 0.3468 at epoch 126 -- collapse happened ~111 epochs *after* the observers froze at iter 60000 (~epoch 174 of ~300, ~99700 iters total), i.e. entirely during the weight-only (no observer recalibration) tail of training. Hypothesis: the 2w+1 transform bakes an unlearnable, unscaled 'sum(x) over the receptive field' term into every conv's integer accumulator (acc = 2*dot(x,w_stored) + sum(x), not just dot(x,w) as before) -- unlike the old w=w scheme, weights can never null this contribution out since it isn't multiplied by anything trainable. If per-channel activation/weight statistics keep drifting after the quantization grid (scale/shift/bias) is frozen, this fixed term's relative weight against the true learned signal can grow and destabilize training. This config only changes quant_freeze_iters 60000 -> 92000 (~92% of the ~99700-iteration budget, vs. the original's ~58%) to shrink that unsupervised drift window from ~126 epochs to ~24, keeping quant_warmup_iters (float32-then-QAT onset) unchanged. Not a proven fix -- a targeted, reversible experiment based on the timing correlation above.
